findings.title: The DELETE column: 39 delete verbs, 6 LIVE, and 27 per-family deleters are rivals to the one live route
findings.measured: node over raw/verbs-parsed.json filtering kind=delete, cross-read against docs/04-reference/API-VERB-REGISTER.md.
findings.detail: 39 of the 361 verbs are delete-shaped. Exactly SIX carry LIVE liveness: element.delete, element.deleteBatch (both owner plugins/view, both routed through the legacy commandManager, chat capabilities delete-selected and delete-furniture-scoped), elementType.delete, room.delete, view.deleteDefinition, viewTemplate.delete. The other 33 are UNKNOWN. NOT ONE delete verb is classified REFUSES — so none of them answers in the open that it will not act.
findings.the_point: Every per-family deleter — wall.delete, slab.delete, door.delete, window.delete, roof.delete, column.delete, beam.delete, ceiling.delete, stair.delete, curtain-wall.delete, furniture.delete, lighting.delete, plumbing.delete, structural.delete, handrail.delete, grid.delete, dimension.delete, annotation.delete, balcony.delete, lift.delete, pool.delete, bathroomPod.delete, boundaryLine.delete, section.delete, sheet.delete, schedule.delete, view.delete — is UNKNOWN, while element.delete IS live. These are not 27 gaps. They are 27 RIVALS to a working route, already minted.
findings.why_it_has_never_been_measured_here: The 2026-08-29 audit measured ONE verb per family, and that verb was create.
findings.ladder: AUTHORED yes / REACHABLE unproven for 33 of 39 / COMPOSABLE not established / CERTIFIED no.
findings.corroboration: tools/ga-gate/mirror-debt.json (quoted in the 2026-08-29 pool row): "~23 rows on this ledger are *.delete and they all need the same one thing — an element.deleted channel plus a per-family remove(id) adapter." Consistent with, and independent of, this measurement.

findings.detail: structural.created 0 · slab.layer-updated 0 · room.created 0 · plumbing.created 0 · grid.created 0 · floor.layer-updated 0 · dimension.created 0 · ceiling.layer-updated 0 · annotation.created 0. Eight of the nine appear nowhere in the repository except the emit site and the RuntimeEvents key declaration in packages/runtime-composer/src/types.ts.
findings.the_point: slab.layer-updated, ceiling.layer-updated and floor.layer-updated are emitted by the CEB cases slab.updateLayers (:1613), ceiling.updateLayers (:1633) and floor.updateLayers (:1653) — three of only four non-create cases in the entire switch. The bridge’s update arm exists, is reached, and emits into nothing.
findings.the_ninth: room.created is the interesting one. It has three further sites and none is a subscription: initCollaboration.ts:68 is a label map, PlatformProjectBrowser.ts:991 is a webhook allowlist, and packages/stores/src/aggregate-commands/roomCreate.ts:111 + types.ts:347 declare a SAME-NAMED event on a DIFFERENT bus. A cross-bus name collision, not a listener.
findings.ladder: AUTHORED yes / REACHABLE yes (the emit runs) / COMPOSABLE no — nothing consumes it / CERTIFIED no.

findings.title: REFUTATION — the DeleteStairCommand opening defect the code still cites as current is CLOSED, but the fix lives on the legacy side of a rival pair
findings.measured: grep -n for opening/Opening over packages/command-registry/src/stair/DeleteStairCommand.ts, comment lines excluded → 22 non-comment references; and the full text of plugins/stair/src/handlers/DeleteStair.ts (37 lines).
findings.the_claim: apps/editor/src/engine/bathroomPodMemberMirror.ts:44 names "the DeleteStairCommand defect (zero references to openings, void left punched through the plate forever)" in the present tense.
findings.the_measurement: FALSE as written. DeleteStairCommand.ts declares affectedStores = ["stair","opening","slab","handrail","floor","ceiling"] (:54), collects its auto-openings via isStairAutoOpeningId (:354-356), removes them and unregisters them from bimManager and elementRegistry (:360-363), and RESTORES them from _openingSnapshots on undo (:421-429). The cascade is there and it is undo-symmetric.
findings.the_part_that_survives: That fix is in the LEGACY packages/command-registry command. plugins/stair/src/handlers/DeleteStair.ts — the handler that owns the BUS verb stair.delete (UNKNOWN liveness) — is 37 lines, declares affectedStores = ["stair"], and contains ZERO references to openings. So there are two stair deleters: one that cascades correctly and one that leaves the void. This is P1-F1 in miniature, with the correct behaviour on the side the new architecture is migrating AWAY from.
findings.doctrine: A refutation is a success mode. Reported, cited, and not padded into a finding it is not.

findings.title: check-verb-register.ts is RED, and the list that rotted is inside the gate
findings.detail: Four failures. V2 finds the committed register STALE on exactly ONE line — line 18, "1407 files read" vs 1408 — while all 361 verb rows match, which is why that artefact is usable as the verb authority here. V4 finds the gate’s OWN in-source named baselines 18 rows out of date in both directions: 1 new SHADOWED (sheet.create — a second registration site that initBusHandlers.ts:2202 skips), 13 new UNKNOWN (balcony ×3, bathroomPod ×2, boundaryLine ×5, lift ×2, room.setColourMode), and 5 rows that no longer qualify (beam/furniture/lighting/plumbing .changeLevel, sheet.create).
findings.the_point: C69 §3 forbids a transcribed verb list because such lists rot. The GENERATED artefact held. The hand-maintained list that rotted is the one INSIDE the gate that enforces the rule.
